papers.title: Investigation of chessboard scanning strategy in selective laser melting of ti6al4v
papers.abstract: Selective Laser Melting (SLM) is recognized as a technology capable of producing metallic components with advantages in geometric flexibility and consistency of mechanical properties. mong the various alloys processed through SLM, titanium alloy Ti6Al4V is particularly attractive due to its superior strength-to-weight ratio, corrosion resistance, and thermal stability. Nevertheless, the quality of as-SLM Ti6Al4V parts is strongly affected by the selection of process parameters. In particular, the laser scanning strategy plays a decisive role in governing energy distribution, thermal gradients, and subsequent microstructural evolution during fabrication. One of the scanning approaches, the chessboard strategy, has gained significant attention because it subdivides the building area into smaller islands that are scanned alternately, reducing scan length and promoting more uniform heat distribution. This study investigates the application of the chessboard strategy in fabricating cylindrical Ti6Al4V specimens, with process maintained constantly. The fabricated geometry exhibited good agreement with the original design, confirming the capability of SLM to reproduce complex features under controlled conditions. Surface characterization revealed protrusions on the top surface (upskin), attributed to excess energy accumulation at the end of scan tracks, while fine wavy-bulgy patterns were observed on the lateral surfaces due to overlapping melt pools and re-solidified particles. The measured average surface roughness (Ra) was 4.275 ± 0.655 µm, falling within an acceptable range for SLM-fabricated components. In addition, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analysis revealed the presence of lack-of-fusion porosity, indicating localized imperfections in powder melting and consolidation. Overall, the findings highlight that the chessboard scanning strategy not only influences thermal distribution but also directly affects surface morphology and porosity characteristics, providing essential insights for optimizing as-SLM Ti6Al4V.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了Ti6Al4V的SLM棋盘扫描策略对表面粗糙度和孔隙的影响，但未涉及任何力学或疲劳性能，与L1方向的核心关注点关联较弱。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not report any mechanical or fatigue properties (tensile, fatigue, hardness) or modeling; it only focuses on scanning strategy effects on surface roughness and porosity without linking to mechanical performance.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究SLM中棋盘扫描策略对Ti6Al4V成形质量的影响。
summary_zh.method: 采用棋盘扫描策略制造圆柱试样，进行表面粗糙度和SEM分析。
summary_zh.result: 表面粗糙度Ra=4.275±0.655µm，观察到熔合不良孔隙。
summary_zh.validation: 通过表面形貌和SEM实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of chessboard scanning strategy on the quality of SLM-fabricated Ti6Al4V parts.
summary_en.method: Cylindrical Ti6Al4V specimens were fabricated using the chessboard scanning strategy and characterized by surface roughness measurements and SEM.
summary_en.result: The average surface roughness was 4.275 ± 0.655 µm, and lack-of-fusion porosity was observed.
summary_en.validation: The findings were validated through experimental surface characterization and SEM analysis.

papers.title: Pengembangan gear dengan proses additive manufacturing berbasis lattice structure dengan dimensi variasional
papers.abstract: Gears are fundamental components in mechanical systems, where reducing weight without compromising strength is a key engineering challenge. This study introduces a multi-material gear with a lattice structure fabricated by Additive Manufacturing (AM). The design integrates an outer gear of Ti-6Al-4V for high strength and wear resistance with an inner gear of 316L stainless steel for structural support. Weight reduction was achieved by generating a diamond wire cube lattice with variable strut diameters, optimized using stress distribution data from finite element analysis and clustering with the K-means algorithm. Structural analysis through ANSYS Explicit Dynamics and fatigue simulations confirmed that stresses remained below the ultimate tensile strength of both materials, ensuring reliable service life. Thermal analysis with CFD indicated a maximum operating temperature of 64.1 °C, within the typical gear range of 50–140 °C. The proposed design reduces gear mass by 34.8% compared to a solid model, demonstrating the feasibility of multi-material AM with lattice optimization for lightweight and durable gear applications.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究的是齿轮而非股骨柄假体，不涉及骨科植入物结构设计或力学性能。
llm.why_not_core: The paper studies a multi-material gear, not a femoral/hip stem or orthopaedic implant; there is no biomechanical analysis, stress shielding, or implant-related performance evaluation.

summary_zh.motivation: 为减轻齿轮重量同时保持强度，提出多材料点阵结构设计。
summary_zh.method: 采用Ti-6Al-4V外齿轮和316L内齿轮，结合点阵结构和K-means聚类优化。
summary_zh.result: 齿轮减重34.8%，应力和温度均在安全范围内。
summary_zh.validation: 通过有限元分析验证结构强度和疲劳寿命，无实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To achieve weight reduction in gears without sacrificing strength by employing additive manufacturing and lattice structures.
summary_en.method: A multi-material gear design with an outer Ti-6Al-4V ring and inner 316L support, incorporating a diamond wire cube lattice with variable strut diameters optimized via finite element analysis and K-means clustering.
summary_en.result: The optimized gear achieves a 34.8% mass reduction while maintaining stresses below the ultimate tensile strength of both materials and a maximum operating temperature of 64.1 °C.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed through finite element analysis (static, fatigue, and thermal CFD) without experimental testing.

papers.title: A design framework for additively manufactured Ti–6Al–4V cervical corpectomy cage combining standardized topology-optimized core and customized lattice interfaces
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) enables the integration of topology-optimized load-bearing architectures with lattice-based contact surfaces, offering new opportunities to tailor the mechanical performance of metallic spinal implants. In this study, a Ti-6Al-4V AM cervical corpectomy fusion (PCCF) cage with a weighted topology-optimized core and customized lattice contact surfaces was developed. Finite element analysis and topology optimization under triaxial physiological loading conditions were employed to define the optimal material distribution, resulting in a load-bearing outer shell with a lightweight, hollow interior suitable for bone grafting. The superior and inferior contact surfaces were reconstructed from patient CT data and integrated with a bionic lattice to promote osseointegration. Experimental validation was performed using static compression, fatigue, and subsidence tests in accordance with ASTM F2077-22 and ASTM F2267-22, benchmarked against ISO 23089-2. The PCCF cage exhibited an axial stiffness of 7397.93 ± 142.62 N/mm and a yield load of 8250.79 ± 281.92 N, exceeding ISO reference values, and withstood 5,000,000 cycles of axial (1582 N) and torsional (1.0 N·m) loading without structural failure. Subsidence testing yielded a stiffness (Kp) of 476.06 ± 52.97 N/mm, approximately 1.85 times higher than the ISO benchmark, indicating improved load distribution at the bone–implant interface. In vitro cell viability testing further showed higher metabolic activity on the lattice surface than on a solid surface. The proposed design framework was demonstrated using a customized C3–C6 PCCF cage as a representative case study, highlighting the potential of AM as a design-enabling approach for mechanically robust and subsidence-resistant spinal implants.

papers.title: The property of a root-extended Ti-6Al-4V endocrown utilizing 3D printing for a four-wall defect in endodontically treated molars: An in vitro study
papers.abstract: Severely damaged molars pose significant challenges in restorative dentistry. Conventional methods, such as resin composite restorations, often fail to provide sufficient fracture resistance, marginal integrity, and sealing, leading to frequent failures and secondary caries. This study aims to compare the mechanical properties and marginal integrity of 3D-printed Ti-6Al-4V root-extended endocrowns with direct resin composite restorations in molars with 4-wall defects. Forty-two extracted third molars were randomly assigned to a 3D-printed Ti-6Al-4V root-extended endocrown group (n = 21) or a nanohybrid resin composite group (n = 21). All specimens underwent thermocycling. Fracture resistance was evaluated in eight specimens per group using vertical loading. Microleakage was assessed by methylene blue staining, and marginal integrity was evaluated by SEM. Micro-CT was performed on endocrown specimens without visible failure to detect internal microcracks. The endocrown group showed a significantly higher fracture resistance than the resin group (4682 ± 981 N vs. 1334 ± 615 N, P < 0.05). No catastrophic failures occurred in the endocrown group, whereas the resin group exhibited multiple failure modes. Lower microleakage scores and fewer marginal defects were observed in the endocrown group (P < 0.05). Micro-CT revealed limited microcracks in two endocrown specimens, and marginal gaps remained within clinically acceptable limits. The study innovatively designs a 3D-printed Ti-6Al-4V root-extended endocrown, combining the structural advantages of endocrowns and post-core restorations. In our study, the 3D-printed Ti-6Al-4V root-extended endocrowns exhibited markedly enhanced fracture resistance, diminished microleakage, improved marginal integrity in comparison to the direct resin restorations, hence endorsing their application for molars with severe defect.

summary_zh.method: 体外实验，对42颗离体第三磨牙进行垂直加载断裂测试、微渗漏评估和SEM/Micro-CT分析。
summary_zh.result: Ti-6Al-4V牙冠断裂强度显著高于树脂组（4682 vs 1334 N），微渗漏更低，边缘完整性更好。
summary_zh.validation: 通过断裂力学测试、染料渗入和显微成像验证。

summary_en.motivation: To compare the mechanical properties and marginal integrity of 3D-printed Ti-6Al-4V root-extended endocrowns versus direct resin composite restorations in molars with severe defects.
summary_en.method: An in vitro study on 42 extracted third molars, assessing fracture resistance via vertical loading, microleakage by methylene blue staining, and marginal integrity by SEM and micro-CT.
summary_en.result: The Ti-6Al-4V endocrowns exhibited significantly higher fracture resistance (4682 vs 1334 N), lower microleakage, and better marginal integrity than resin restorations.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing, dye penetration, and microscopic imaging.
